propositions.name: species_law_coincident
propositions.quote: Every species has come into existence coincident both in space and time with a pre-existing closely allied species.
propositions.statement: Every species has come into existence coincident in space and time with a pre-existing closely allied species.

propositions.name: each_species_has_antitype
propositions.quote: each one having had for its immediate antitype a closely allied species existing at the time of its origin
propositions.statement: Each species has had for its immediate antitype a closely allied species existing at the time of its origin.

propositions.name: no_species_appears_twice
propositions.quote: no group or species has come into existence twice
propositions.statement: No group or species has come into existence twice.

propositions.name: complete_renewal_several_times
propositions.quote: This complete renewal of the forms of life also appears to have occurred several times
propositions.statement: The complete renewal of the forms of life has occurred several times.

propositions.name: gradual_extinction_and_creation
propositions.quote: the present condition of the organic world is clearly derived by a natural process of gradual extinction and creation of species
propositions.statement: The present organic world is derived by a natural process of gradual extinction and creation of species.

propositions.name: surface_of_earth_changes
propositions.quote: during an immense, but unknown period, the surface of the earth has undergone successive changes
propositions.statement: The surface of the earth has undergone successive changes over an immense but unknown period.

propositions.name: affinities_branching_line
propositions.quote: the series of affinities will be compound, and can only be represented by a forked or many-branched line
propositions.statement: When multiple species share a common antitype, the series of affinities is compound and represented by a forked or many-branched line.

propositions.name: isolation_produces_peculiar_groups
propositions.quote: A country having species, genera, and whole families peculiar to it, will be the necessary result of its having been isolated for a long period
propositions.statement: A country's peculiar species, genera, and families are the necessary result of long isolation permitting many series of species to form.

propositions.name: allied_species_geographically_near
propositions.quote: the most closely allied species are found in the same locality or in closely adjoing localities; and that therefore the natural sequence of the species by affinity is also geographical
propositions.statement: Most closely allied species are found in the same or closely adjoining localities, so affinity sequence is also geographical.

propositions.name: representative_species_across_barriers
propositions.quote: In countries of a similar climate, but separated by a wide sea of lofty mountains, the families, genera and species of the one are often represented by closely allied families, genera and species peculiar to the other
propositions.statement: Similar climates separated by sea or mountains often have closely allied representative families, genera, and species peculiar to each.

propositions.name: time_distribution_mirrors_space
propositions.quote: The distribution of the organic world in time is very similar to its present distribution in space
propositions.statement: The distribution of the organic world in time is very similar to its present distribution in space.

propositions.name: same_period_species_more_allied
propositions.quote: Species of one genus, or genera of one family occurring in the same geological time are more closely allied than those separated in time
propositions.statement: Species and genera of the same geological time are more closely allied than those separated in time.

propositions.name: conditions_render_species_impossible
propositions.quote: Geological changes, however gradual, must occasionally have modified external conditions to such an extent as to have rendered the existence of certain species impossible
propositions.statement: Geological changes must occasionally have modified external conditions enough to render the existence of certain species impossible.

propositions.name: extinction_gradual_or_sudden
propositions.quote: The extinction would in most cases be affected by a gradual dying-out, but in some instances there might have been a sudden destruction of a species of limited range
propositions.statement: Extinction is usually a gradual dying-out but may sometimes be sudden for species of limited range.

propositions.name: rudimentary_organs_no_function
propositions.quote: That these really do exist, and in most cases have no special function in the animal æconomy, is admitted by the first authorities in comparative anatomy
propositions.statement: Rudimentary organs really do exist and in most cases have no special function in the animal economy.

propositions.name: every_change_must_be_gradual
propositions.quote: the great law which has regulated the peopling of the earth with animal and vegetable life is, that every change shall be gradual; that no new creature shall be formed widely differing from anything before existing
propositions.statement: The great law is that every change shall be gradual, so no new creature is formed widely differing from anything before existing.

propositions.name: fossil_knowledge_fragmentary
propositions.quote: our knowledge of the whole series of the former inhabitants of the earth is necessarily most imperfect and fragmentary
propositions.statement: Our knowledge of the whole series of former inhabitants of the earth is necessarily most imperfect and fragmentary.

propositions.name: formations_buried_beneath_ocean
propositions.quote: whole formations containing the records of vast geological periods are: entirely buried beneath the ocean, and for ever beyond our reach
propositions.statement: Whole formations recording vast geological periods are entirely buried beneath the ocean and beyond our reach.

propositions.name: theory_of_gradual_change
propositions.quote: though it may appear to some readers essentially a theory of progression, it is in reality only one of gradual change
propositions.statement: The hypothesis is in reality only one of gradual change rather than essentially a theory of progression.

propositions.name: recent_islands_lack_peculiars
propositions.quote: no example is known of an island which can be proved geologically to be of very recent origin (late in the Tertiary, for instance), and yet possesses generic or family groups, or even many species peculiar to itself
propositions.statement: No geologically very recent island possesses generic or family groups or many species peculiar to itself.

propositions.name: galapagos_populated_by_dispersal
propositions.quote: They must have been first peopled, like other newly-formed islands, by the action of winds and currents, and at a period sufficiently remote to have had the original species die out, and the modified prototypes only remain
propositions.statement: The Galapagos were first peopled by winds and currents at a period remote enough for original species to die out and modified prototypes to remain.

propositions.name: quiescence_favors_abundance
propositions.quote: a long period of quiescence or stability in the physical conditions of a district would be most favourable to the existence of organic life in the greatest abundance
propositions.statement: A long period of quiescence or stability in physical conditions is most favourable to the greatest abundance and variety of organic life.

propositions.name: analogy_becomes_affinity_near_antitype
propositions.quote: as we go back along the parallel or divergent series, towards the common antitype, the analogy which existed between the two groups becomes an affinity
propositions.statement: Going back along parallel or divergent series toward the common antitype, an analogy between two groups becomes an affinity.

propositions.name: facts_alone_to_disprove
propositions.quote: he expects facts alone to be brought to disprove it; not a à-priori arguments against its probabiliy
propositions.statement: The hypothesis expects facts alone to be brought to disprove it, not a priori arguments against its probability.

propositions.name: widely_distributed_genera_local_groups
propositions.quote: in widely distributed genera, well-marked groups of species are peculiar to each geographical district
propositions.statement: In widely distributed genera, well-marked groups of species are peculiar to each geographical district.

propositions.name: gaps_softened_by_intermediates
propositions.quote: The great gaps that exist between fishes, reptiles, birds and mammals would then, no doubt, be softened down by intermediate groups
propositions.statement: The great gaps between fishes, reptiles, birds and mammals would be softened by intermediate groups if all extinct forms were seen.

propositions.name: natural_series_is_order_of_creation
propositions.quote: it follows that the natural series of affinities will also represent the order in which the several species came into existence
propositions.statement: The natural series of affinities represents the order in which the several species came into existence.

propositions.name: lower_forms_survive_to_reseed
propositions.quote: whenever any of the higher groups have become nearly or quite extinct, the lower forms which have better resisted the modified physical conditions have served as the antitypes on which to found the new races
propositions.statement: When higher groups have become nearly extinct, lower forms that have better resisted modified conditions serve as antitypes on which to found the new races.
